maya: quick note — after the kernel-selector change this morning i'm seeing a clear regression on A100 long-seq path.
maya: p90 latency up ~12% for seq=2048 on batch=1, small-batch path.
maya: baseline (old-selector) p90 210ms -> new p90 235ms
akshay: ouch. can you drop the perf trace+nvprof flame?
maya: pasted quick flame (truncated):
```
GPU: a100
kernel: attention_fwd_specialized
time: 87.4ms  (was 62.1ms)
registers per thread: 64 -> 96
shared mem used: 28KB -> 52KB
blocks: 80 -> 56
```
jules: looks like the selector picked a warp-specialized kernel that uses more registers and smem per thread. register pressure -> spill -> slower.
dena: also noticed higher kv-cache misses on that path. prefetch/evict interplay may cause extra mem ops. prefetch increased latency by ~3-4ms on seq>1024.
akshay: can we gate that kernel by occupancy? e.g. require occupancy >= 0.6 else fall back to generic kernel.
maya: +1. quick experiment: forcing generic path reduces p90 back to 212ms but throughput drops slightly.
perf-bot: nightly perf job #4821: regression detected on a100-longseq, delta p90 +11.7% link: https://ci/redwood/perf/4821
jules: proposal: add an autotune rule: for seqlen>=1024 and estimated smem per-block < 40KB allow warp-specialized; else prefer generic. also add register-threshold < 80.
dena: also add kv-cache-prefetch=false for sequences over 1536 for now.
akshay: i'll prototype selector patch, will run canary on dedicated pool.
maya: thanks — i'll attach a small repro script and perf logs in the PR.
